properties.name: Russian programme of re-education and adoption of Ukrainian children (Yale HRL, Feb 2023)
properties.group: Russia's taking of Ukrainian children
properties.placed at: Russia (the middle of the country (a country-wide record))
properties.what: The Yale Humanitarian Research Lab (Conflict Observatory) identified at least 43 facilities holding children from Ukraine: 41 camps (7 in occupied Crimea, 34 in mainland Russia), a psychiatric hospital and a family centre; 32 camps showed re-education activity. It documented at least 6,000 children held, and Russian claims of re-homing and pending adoptions. The report does not publish the full list of camp locations. Figures: At least 43 facilities; at least 6,000 children; 32 camps (78%) with re-education; Lvova-Belova claimed 350 re-homed and over 1,000 awaiting adoption (summer 2022); Ukraine documented over 14,700 deported (26 Jan 2023)

properties.group: Russia's taking of Ukrainian children
properties.placed at: Russia (the middle of the country (a country-wide record))
properties.what: A Yale Humanitarian Research Lab report released 3 December 2024 identified at least 314 children from Ukraine subject to coerced adoption and fostering through Russian child-placement databases, most of them from Donetsk region; at least 67 had been naturalised as Russian citizens. properties.name: Stolen Generations: Bringing Them Home national inquiry (1997)
properties.group: Australia's Stolen Generations
properties.placed at: Australia (the middle of the country (a country-wide record))
properties.what: The National Inquiry into the Separation of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Children from Their Families (Sir Ronald Wilson and Mick Dodson) reported in April 1997 that between one in three and one in ten Indigenous children were forcibly removed between 1910 and 1970, into institutions, foster and adoptive care, and found the practice amounted to genocide under international law. Prime Minister Kevin Rudd apologised on 13 February 2008. Figures: Between 1 in 3 and 1 in 10 children removed 1910–1970; 535 Aboriginal people heard; over 600 submissions

properties.placed at: Darwin (Myilly Point), Northern Territory (the site)
properties.what: Compound set up under NT Protector of Aborigines Walter Baldwin Spencer into which mixed-descent Aboriginal families and children were gathered from 1913; children were moved to the Half-Caste Home at Myilly Point in 1924. It closed in 1939.

properties.name: Retta Dixon Home, Darwin
properties.group: Australia's Stolen Generations
properties.placed at: Darwin, Northern Territory (the town)
properties.what: Home in Darwin run by the Aborigines Inland Mission (now Australian Indigenous Ministries) for Aboriginal children; the Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse examined sexual abuse of children there between 1946 and 1980 (Case Study 17).

properties.name: Colebrook Home, Oodnadatta (Oodnadatta Children's Home)
properties.group: Australia's Stolen Generations
properties.placed at: Oodnadatta, South Australia (the middle of the region named)
properties.what: United Aborigines Mission home for Aboriginal children set up at Oodnadatta under missionary Annie Lock, before moving to Quorn in 1927; former residents identify as members of the Stolen Generations.

properties.name: Colebrook Children's Home, Quorn
properties.group: Australia's Stolen Generations
properties.placed at: Quorn, South Australia (the town)
properties.what: The United Aborigines Mission's Colebrook Children's Home for Aboriginal children operated at Quorn from 1927 to 1944, run by Matron Ruby Hyde and Sister Delia Rutter, then moved to Eden Hills.

properties.name: Colebrook Home, Eden Hills
properties.group: Australia's Stolen Generations
properties.placed at: Eden Hills, South Australia (the town)
properties.what: The United Aborigines Mission's Colebrook Home for Aboriginal children operated at Eden Hills near Adelaide from 1944 until 1981; former residents identify as members of the Stolen Generations. The site is now Colebrook Blackwood Reconciliation Park.

properties.name: Moore River Native Settlement
properties.group: Australia's Stolen Generations
properties.placed at: Moore River Native Settlement, Western Australia (the middle of the region named)
properties.what: Settlement north of Perth to which Aboriginal children removed from their families were sent; it is the setting of the Rabbit-Proof Fence account of three girls who ran away from it.

properties.name: Indian Adoption Project (Child Welfare League of America)
properties.group: Native American children adopted out
properties.placed at: Western United States (the middle of the country (a country-wide record))
properties.what: Federally funded project run by the Child Welfare League of America with the Bureau of Indian Affairs and the US Children's Bureau that placed 395 Native American children from 16 western states with white adoptive families, mainly in Illinois, Indiana, New York, Massachusetts and Missouri. CWLA executive director Shay Bilchik apologised in June 2001, saying it 'was wrong; it was hurtful'. Figures: 395 children placed by 31 Dec 1967 (119 in 1967); over 5,000 prospective adoptive families referred; about 50 cooperating agencies

properties.name: Indian Child Welfare Act (1978): pre-ICWA removal of Native children
properties.group: Native American children adopted out
properties.placed at: Washington, D.C., District of Columbia (the town)
properties.what: Congress passed the Indian Child Welfare Act in 1978 after hearings found 'the wholesale separation of Indian children from their families'; a survey before the Act reported that about 25–35% of all Indian children were separated from their families and placed in foster homes, adoptive homes or institutions, at high rates with non-Indians. Figures: Approximately 25–35 percent of all Indian children separated

properties.name: 'Little Danes' experiment: 22 Inuit children shipped from Nuuk
properties.group: Greenland's little Danes
properties.placed at: Nuuk, Sermersooq (the town)
properties.what: In May 1951 22 Greenlandic Inuit children (13 boys, 9 girls), selected by priests and mostly not orphans, sailed from Nuuk to Denmark to be raised as Danish speakers; six were adopted by Danish families and 16 returned to a Danish-speaking orphanage in Greenland. Denmark apologised in 2020 and in March 2022 paid each of six survivors 250,000 kroner. Figures: 22 children; 6 adopted in Denmark; 16 returned; 250,000 DKK to each of 6 survivors

properties.name: Fedgaarden camp, Feddet: Greenlandic children quarantined before Danish foster homes
properties.group: Greenland's little Danes
properties.placed at: Feddet, Zealand (the middle of the region named)
properties.what: The 22 Greenlandic children of the 1951 experiment were first held for the summer at a Save the Children 'holiday camp' at Fedgaarden on the Feddet peninsula, then placed with Danish foster families for over a year; six were adopted. The project was run with the Red Cross and Save the Children. Figures: 22 children
